```plato
    //==
    // # The zero matrix, per concrete type
    //
    // `IAdditive.Zero` cannot be derived generically here for the same reason
    // Transpose cannot (see the TODO above): it must CONSTRUCT a matrix, and
    // IMatrix exposes no construction primitive. So each concrete type
    // supplies its own, exactly as the note above prescribes. The fixed-size
    // types are TYPE-TOKEN members (`_` receiver: reachable as Matrix2x2.Zero
    // or off any value); their shape is static, so the rows are written out
    // literally. MatrixN carries its shape at runtime and so must keep a real
    // receiver, rebuilding a zero-filled component array from it.
    // (Zero lives on IAdditive, not INumericalLimits.)

    // The 2x2 matrix with every element zero (the additive identity).
    Zero(_: Matrix2x2): Matrix2x2
        => ((0.0, 0.0), (0.0, 0.0));
```

## Line 621

```plato

    // The zero matrix of the receiver's shape; the runtime shape is copied from
    // the receiver, so this is the additive identity for that shape only.
    Zero(x: MatrixN): MatrixN
        => (x.NumRows, x.NumColumns, x.ElementCount.MapRange(k => 0.0));
```
